newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFin bonds hit record on debt talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFin bonds hit record on debt talks.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds rose to new highs on healthy volumes on Wednesday as the market welcomed the outcome of a meeting between Russia and the London Club of commercial bank-creditors representatives, dealers said.
A Moscow Narodny Bank dealer forecast some profit-taking in the next few days on the gains, if U.S. Treasuries are sluggish. If the U.S. bond rises, MinFins will continue to rise, he said.
A Western bank dealer said there was a high chance of a fall, as MinFins' spread over U.S. Treasuries was becoming too narrow.
"When you compare it to other instruments, you already have to think which is more profitable," he said.
Dealers said they had pushed up MinFin prices through the day.
"There was strong growth from the morning on expectations of the news on the London Club," said an International Moscow Bank dealer, speaking before the news about the meeting appeared.

Russia's Finance Ministry and Vneshekonombank officials met with London Club representatives on Wednesday. After the meeting Russia's First Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said the volume of fully reconciled debt was nearing 65 percent.
He also denied market rumours that Russia was going to ask the London Club to cut the threshold of fully reconciled debt necessary to close the restructuring agreement.
London Club news primarily affects the Vnesh debt market, but MinFins follow the trend as an instrument representing Russia's foreign debt.
The Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said the market rose by 0.25 basis points after the news. "The market took it very positively," the dealer said.
He also said there was market talk that Russia's credit rating would be upgraded this autumn, which helped prices rise.
